alignment_check.scope: All 838 source/English pairs read in order, including repeated lines and page transitions; lexical corrections checked individually. No independent expert review.

notes.manas-2010:p0440:b001:l001: Mountain and bundle images in lines 1–3 are retained as corpse heaps; these are not numerical units. Continues the horse description on page 439.
notes.manas-2010:p0440:b001:l017: Мойноп: struggling to break loose, supported by Yudakhin and the 1969 explanatory dictionary at https://el-sozduk.kg/МОЙНО/. No unsupported riding maneuver is specified.
notes.manas-2010:p0440:b001:l025: Аманат жан is life entrusted to a person; чопчогуу is carried into the following English line as utterly. The two source display lines remain separately aligned.
notes.manas-2010:p0440:b001:l027: Кошу ооп колжоктоп is visually present. Loads tipping and dangling is a provisional contextual reading; кошу may refer to baggage/camp equipment and the precise object remains uncertain. Raw reading is not repaired.
notes.manas-2010:p0440:b001:l033: Кыраан applied to the two heroes is retained as falcons, a praise image, not a separate rank.
notes.manas-2010:p0440:b001:l045: Бакалап means watching/looking out, not throttling; Yudakhin and explanatory dictionaries at https://el-sozduk.kg/бакала/. Their course is contextual to the pursuit, not an additional source noun.
notes.manas-2010:p0441:b001:l012: Эригип is a restless/bored state; the negative in аянбай explicitly concerns holding back. Draft wording does not establish a separate event of fatigue. This emotional linkage remains provisional.
notes.manas-2010:p0441:b003:l001: Start of the speech after the two-line editorial heading; the heading is preserved separately in this descriptor and is not counted as verse.
notes.manas-2010:p0441:b003:l012: Он экиде is read as age twelve, not twelve shots. No birth date is inferred.
notes.manas-2010:p0441:b003:l014: Printed кыраңча is irregular; falcon follows the nearby recurring кыраан praise formula, including page 442. This is a contextual reading, not a silent source correction.
notes.manas-2010:p0441:b003:l018: Карыпчы: armguard, following the shared lexicon and https://el-sozduk.kg/КАРЫПЧЫ/. The relation between the khan and this equipment remains the source epithet.
notes.manas-2010:p0442:b001:l024: Баашалуу is visually present; with a ruler provisionally reads it as a form related to пааша. The initial consonant is not repaired in the source.
notes.manas-2010:p0442:b001:l036: The six-thousand expression is preserved. The surrounding horse praise does not establish a modern breed or measured racing field.
notes.manas-2010:p0443:b001:l007: Printed байда is contextually read as пайда, benefit. Source raw text remains unchanged.
notes.manas-2010:p0443:b001:l017: The insulting opposition between courage and lack of intelligence is retained; this is a character’s hostile assessment of Manas.
notes.manas-2010:p0443:b001:l022: Күрмө: a sleeveless outer coat/short jacket, checked in Yudakhin and explanatory dictionary at https://el-sozduk.kg/күрмө/.
notes.manas-2010:p0444:b001:l003: Толгон айза имерди can suggest many spears or a sweeping spear movement; the draft chooses the movement in the individual fighter’s context. The precise construction remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0444:b001:l016: Эңдирип has a causative/transitive shape; the defeat is rendered contextually with the speakers as sufferers. Exact agent relation remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0444:b001:l036: Аярым is interpreted contextually as sparing/mercy in the command not to hold back; a relation to аяр, magician/cunning, is possible. This reading requires specialist review.
notes.manas-2010:p0445:b001:l011: Саадак may denote bow equipment or a quiver. Bow is chosen in the immediate aiming-and-shooting command; it is not mechanically glossed as quiver.
notes.manas-2010:p0445:b001:l022: Кызыталак is an abusive sexual/kinship insult; bastard is an English invective equivalent, not a genealogical assertion.
notes.manas-2010:p0445:b001:l039: Seven thousand is explicit. Сан is retained as san, an epic multitude expression; no exact numerical value is invented for that second term.
notes.manas-2010:p0446:b001:l004: Кол байлап is rendered with the image of tying up hands; figurative hampering is possible in the coordinated attack.
notes.manas-2010:p0446:b001:l015: Каркыбар is a valiant-hero praise term in this context, following the shared lexicon; no new animal or person is introduced.
notes.manas-2010:p0446:b001:l021: Depriving him of wings is retained as the source image; the preceding lines connect this to taking away his horse.
notes.manas-2010:p0446:b001:l038: Күрмө again means sleeveless coat; see the lexical note on page 443 line 22.
notes.manas-2010:p0447:b001:l004: Луңтуң is treated as a title, not a new personal name. J. Tumenbaeva cites the Kyrgyz-Russian dictionary’s village headman and also a district-governor gloss: https://nbisu.moy.su/_ld/10/1088_Tumenbaeva_J.A..pdf. English selects village headmen; the exact hierarchy and the coordination with кандары remain uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0447:b001:l007: Кендери literally suggests mines/treasuries; treasuries of wisdom preserves that image rather than silently replacing it with кандары, khans.
notes.manas-2010:p0447:b001:l029: The source question mark and interrogative force are retained; it is not silently rewritten as a declarative vow to die.
notes.manas-2010:p0447:b001:l039: Ардыккандан is read as from exhaustion, close to ардык-. The warriors’ subsequent agitation does not justify silently changing it to an honor/shame expression.
notes.manas-2010:p0448:b001:l001: Амыз is visually present; honor provisionally follows намыс in the surrounding oath and shame context. The missing initial consonant is not repaired in the retained source.
notes.manas-2010:p0448:b001:l007: Саадак is rendered as bow equipment here; bow/quiver distinction is context-dependent and requires review.
notes.manas-2010:p0448:b001:l015: Hiding behind half a dry stalk is the hyperbolic skill of concealment attributed to the marksman; the impossible scale is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0448:b001:l016: Жаман айтса таңылбас is obscure. The draft provisionally preserves the idea that ill spoken of him would not attach; syntax and its link to the marksmanship praise remain uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0448:b001:l017: Жакшы сүрө бутадан is visually present but syntactically uncertain. Well-tracked target is provisional; the draft does not replace it with a reconstructed standard archery formula.
notes.manas-2010:p0448:b001:l030: The measuring of ground is retained literally; no distance or tactical geometry is added.
notes.manas-2010:p0448:b001:l039: Ардан is irregular. A thousand apiece is provisional from the distributive context; the species/object of slaughter is not explicit. This may contain corruption of аттан (horses), but the draft does not assert that repair. The oath in the next line is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0449:b001:l007: Амызданып is interpreted through намыстанып, having honor/shame aroused. This contextual reading does not modify raw source.
notes.manas-2010:p0449:b001:l011: Ардан is irregular and may conceal аттан, from horses. English preserves slaughter for provisions without inventing stores or a confirmed species; the unclear modifier remains noted here.
notes.manas-2010:p0449:b001:l015: Сан is interpreted as a multitude adjective here, countless; no modern troop count is calculated.
notes.manas-2010:p0449:b003:l003: Ат кара тил: horses’ tongues turning black is the traditional seasonal expression associated with grazing in early summer. Its concrete image is retained, not converted to a calendar date.
notes.manas-2010:p0449:b003:l004: Өң тулпардын is read provisionally as all the tulpars in the grazing/fattening passage; the initial word is unusual and raw text is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0449:b003:l010: Wind, flood and canopy are retained as the source’s protection imagery. The apparent mismatch is not harmonized.
notes.manas-2010:p0449:b003:l015: Эшен is a religious/spiritual master, not a military rank or merely personal piety.
notes.manas-2010:p0450:b001:l006: Ордолугу is rendered as possessing a princely court. The praise may also evoke leadership and ordered household; no palace location is added.
notes.manas-2010:p0450:b001:l022: Калыйпа is rendered as caliph; in this Sufi/religious setting it may mean a deputy or spiritual authority. No historical caliph or date is identified. Entering his presence is a contextual reading of кирип.
notes.manas-2010:p0450:b001:l024: Corrected after individual source PDF image/context review: primary Yudakhin кол entry quotes exact он эки бирге кол берген as being a follower of twelve ishans/spiritual guides. Religious кол бер- expresses subject becoming disciple, not twelve others offering their hands. Guide identities unspecified. Primary dictionary https://kotormo.kg/sites/default/files/2025-02/sozduk_yudahin.pdf cached sources/raw/yudakhin-2015.pdf.
notes.manas-2010:p0450:b001:l026: Зайыппуруш is an exceptional renown/heroic fame epithet, not a personal name or mechanical literal compound. See shared lexical finding and https://el-sozduk.kg/зайыппуруш/.
notes.manas-2010:p0450:b001:l036: Билгенге is visibly printed, literally to the knowing one. Bilerik is named two lines above and may be intended, but the draft does not silently replace this defective reading with his name.
notes.manas-2010:p0450:b001:l038: Карадөң is Karadöng; Жарманас is Jar Manas, distinct from Jakyp’s son Manas. The source’s mistaken identification in the following lines is preserved.
notes.manas-2010:p0451:b001:l003: The rhetorical self-curse invokes Koshoy’s worthiness of his name; it is not translated as a new person or change of identity.
notes.manas-2010:p0451:b001:l007: Чөөлүк- means become exhausted/enfeebled (Yudakhin, https://kotormo.kg/sites/default/files/2025-02/sozduk_yudahin.pdf). Filling the belly follows the source; hunger is not inserted as the definition of the verb.
notes.manas-2010:p0451:b001:l013: Seventy doors is retained here, distinct from sixty gates on page 450 and later in this speech. No numerical harmonization.
notes.manas-2010:p0451:b001:l014: Seven rounds and, in line 16, seven years are both retained as distinct expressions; they are not collapsed into one campaign duration.
notes.manas-2010:p0451:b001:l021: The self-curse about sinking unborn is retained despite its impossible temporal image.
notes.manas-2010:p0451:b001:l033: Шай колдогон expresses favorable/holy protection; the shared dictionary finding links this formula to holy patronage, not to drinking tea or equipment.
notes.manas-2010:p0451:b001:l037: Өлчөсөм is visibly printed and read as weighing/considering. Өлсөм, if I die, is a plausible alternative in this mortality passage, but is not silently substituted.
notes.manas-2010:p0452:b001:l007: Каканчын is retained as Kakan-Chin, an epic designation; no modern state border is inferred.
notes.manas-2010:p0452:b001:l027: Chewing white wheat flour is retained literally as part of the oath context. The draft does not add baking or a loaf.
notes.manas-2010:p0452:b001:l028: Ак куран is rendered as holy Quran; holding the Quran belongs to the oath narrative.
notes.manas-2010:p0452:b001:l029: The sugar tied in a belt is retained. The possessor is not explicit enough to identify with certainty.
notes.manas-2010:p0452:b001:l031: Кудайлашкан антым is an oath sworn with God invoked; no new legal relationship is inferred.
notes.manas-2010:p0453:b001:l018: Өлөң is a song/verse term in Aydarkan’s Kazakh portrayal. The sound and repetition remain in the verse, without inventing a specific song.
notes.manas-2010:p0453:b001:l026: Кембайлап is leading under escort/in a guarded column, supported by the shared Yudakhin finding for кембай. It is not a personal name.
notes.manas-2010:p0453:b001:l031: Bukhara and Andijan are both retained in the adjacent description of Aykhozho. They are not harmonized into a single birthplace.
notes.manas-2010:p0453:b001:l033: Курун селде чалынып: his sash serves as the turban material; the source’s concrete clothing action is preserved.
notes.manas-2010:p0454:b001:l002: Күлазык is travel/campaign provisions. No unsupported ingredient list is inserted.
notes.manas-2010:p0454:b001:l009: Калыйпа repeats the religious authority title from page 450; caliph remains a provisional contextual gloss, with spiritual deputy also possible.
notes.manas-2010:p0454:b001:l010: Касаба туу is rendered as a tasselled standard; the exact kind and ornamentation of касаба remain uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0454:b001:l023: The statement that not one remained is preserved; later twelve sentries and forty guards are not used to revise it.
notes.manas-2010:p0454:b001:l025: Source visibly reads Ордо аткан жеринде, which could literally suggest playing ordo. The captivity/rescue context and the Kyrgyz 1984 Karalaev witness’s indexed parallel Ордо жаткан жеринде support at the place where they lay in the pit. This is an explicit contextual correction in English only; raw source is unchanged. Parallel: https://jasulib.org.kg/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/8.-Манас-1-китеп-Саякбай-Каралаев.pdf; parallel is corroborative, not substituted as the batch witness.
notes.manas-2010:p0454:b001:l029: Twelve sentries and forty guards are explicit and separately retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0454:b001:l035: Супа/суп are interpreted as white cloth/shrouding in the wearing/death-defiance formula, not platforms or dawn. The Kyrgyz academic Manas books 6–7 glossary gives СҮП (супа) as white fabric/clothing and includes shrouds; Yudakhin/explanatory dictionaries at https://el-sozduk.kg/суп/ corroborate fabric used for a shroud. Twelve and four remain distinct; no unit length or number of funerals is invented. The precise counting construction and distinction of the two cloth terms remain uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0454:b001:l036: Wearing the cloth in the preceding line is retained as the source’s defiance of death; the draft does not replace this with a generalized courage summary.
notes.manas-2010:p0455:b001:l001: The quoted pacer/booty declarations in lines 1–4 have an abrupt attachment across the page break. The draft leaves the exact antecedent of this unsettled rather than assigning an unsupported horse.
notes.manas-2010:p0455:b001:l005: Базардын, of the bazaar, is visibly printed. Балдардын, of the boys, is likely in context and recurs two lines later, but the draft retains bazaar rather than silently repairing it.
notes.manas-2010:p0455:b001:l019: Ордо is taken as ор + locative, in the pit, following the dungeon rescue, rather than a royal court.
notes.manas-2010:p0455:b001:l025: Керишке эки ат минип is rendered as riding the two horses in turn. The exact adverbial force of керишке remains uncertain; the source does not state simultaneous riding.
notes.manas-2010:p0455:b001:l033: Телжээрде is retained as Telzheerde. It is not silently unified with the differently named Telkyzyl found elsewhere.
notes.manas-2010:p0455:b001:l038: Jar Manas remains the rescued captive distinct from Manas son of Jakyp.
notes.manas-2010:p0456:b001:l006: Чай алган тоо is read descriptively as the mountain where tea was gathered. A place-name reading is possible, but not verified.
notes.manas-2010:p0456:b001:l009: Жан казан is provisionally a camp cauldron in the hearth-digging context. Жан is unusual here; the draft does not silently repair it to чоң, large.
notes.manas-2010:p0456:b001:l011: Ай туяк is the horse-sacrifice expression: https://el-sozduk.kg/tuyak-5/. The literal moon-hoof image is retained alongside offerings; it does not assert actual crescent-shaped hooves.
notes.manas-2010:p0456:b001:l012: Two hundred mares are explicitly preserved; they are not normalized to a more plausible feast size.
notes.manas-2010:p0456:b001:l013: Баабедин is the invoked patron/saint Bahauddin in the shared terminology. Swiftly follows бат; no separate person performing the slaughter is introduced.
notes.manas-2010:p0456:b001:l035: Менде is read as the recurring пенде/бенде, mortal person, in the epic formula. Raw spelling remains unchanged.
notes.manas-2010:p0456:b001:l036: Чалыяр is rendered as the Four Companions, a traditional religious collective; it is not identified as four military allies present in the scene.
notes.manas-2010:p0456:b001:l039: Sulayman is the religious/epic Solomon figure. The statement is a character’s account of Beijing’s exceptional power, not a historical finding.
notes.manas-2010:p0457:b001:l004: The One-Eyed are an epic/fantastic people named in the speech; no modern ethnic identification is made.
notes.manas-2010:p0457:b001:l006: Бейпайлашкан is interpreted as bringing misery/hardship, following the shared dictionary finding for бейпай. The reciprocal/participial force remains contextual.
notes.manas-2010:p0457:b001:l012: Lines 12–16 report Koshoy’s claim about a divine promise; they are not presented as a verified Quranic quotation.
notes.manas-2010:p0457:b001:l017: The last of six lions is preserved as an epic formula; no list of six ancestors is manufactured.
notes.manas-2010:p0457:b001:l024: Binding to the waist is preserved as the image of relying on Manas as support.
notes.manas-2010:p0457:b001:l027: Greasy yurt felt and, in line 31, greasy lattice walls are prosperity/hospitality imagery, not an instruction to damage the dwelling. Shared explanatory-dictionary finding for туурдук.
notes.manas-2010:p0457:b001:l029: Алакандай is literally palm-sized; handful preserves the smallness of the Muslim community addressed without specifying a population.
notes.manas-2010:p0457:b001:l034: The high pass remains a support/protection image applied to Manas, not a newly named geographical location.
notes.manas-2010:p0458:b001:l010: The Black Kalmyks’ complaint and the fierce anger in lines 9–13 have uncertain agent linkage. The draft follows a threat directed against Esenkan, then his reaction, but does not claim the syntax uniquely supports this reading.
notes.manas-2010:p0458:b001:l026: English adds around to maintain the Chinese clans as the subject of каптап жатып калды across lines 25–27. It does not reverse the encirclement and make Manas its agent.
notes.manas-2010:p0458:b001:l032: Жабылалы is visibly an apparent first-person plural imperative. Let us rally is retained as an interruption within the surrounding Creator-gift statement; a damaged collective modifier is possible but not silently substituted.
notes.manas-2010:p0458:b001:l042: The self-sacrifice vow is retained as Koshoy’s war speech, not a narrator recommendation.
notes.manas-2010:p0459:b001:l002: Бубалы is visibly printed. Gird follows the familiar белди бекем буу formula; likely missing consonant is not repaired in the raw witness.
notes.manas-2010:p0459:b001:l003: Кытайды is accusative although the draft reads the Chinese as the eager party; the unusual case/syntax is retained in the source and the English relation is provisional.
notes.manas-2010:p0459:b001:l015: Ооган is retained as the Afghans in the epic geography; no modern political event is asserted.
notes.manas-2010:p0459:b001:l028: Калдай is governor, following the shared lexicon. Кандайдын is visibly printed but irregular; a khan’s is a contextual reading alongside кандыгын, khanate. The raw form is not silently rewritten as кандардын.
notes.manas-2010:p0459:b001:l031: Жая is the horse-rump meat cut; it is not generic meat or a hoof.
notes.manas-2010:p0459:b001:l033: Жаң-жуң is rendered governor-general, following the shared lexicon and Yudakhin-derived title gloss, not left as a new personal name.
notes.manas-2010:p0459:b001:l037: Зулпукор is retained as the named sword Zulpukor; the line also names the black spear. No claim is made that they are the same weapon.
notes.manas-2010:p0459:b001:l038: Көөлөшөрмүн is provisionally wielding/engaging together with the weapons named above; the exact verb form is uncertain and remains unrepaired in raw source.
notes.manas-2010:p0459:b001:l040: Кылым is read contextually as the world/peoples, not a chronological century, in the boast contrasting China with the wider world.
notes.manas-2010:p0459:b001:l042: Open conditional continues on page 460. No conclusion is supplied to make this batch end like a finished episode.
notes.manas-2010:p0443:b001:l024: Lexical correction: таш сайынган means a Chinese/Kalmyk official wearing a distinguishing ball/button on the cap, Yudakhin таш I.5 https://el-sozduk.kg/таш/. In this formula таза means finest, not bald/shaven: Yudakhin таза3 https://el-sozduk.kg/ТАЗ/. Raw source unchanged.

publication_basis: New draft translation directly from Kyrgyz traditional folklore. No prior English translation used. Modern editorial headings are retained for audit only; no independent Kyrgyz specialist review or complete-witness claim.
